title: Private/VPC & On-Prem Packaging experiments: pricing, support tiers, upgrade cadence + Security QA
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Run a set of product and commercial experiments to define: 1) a baseline license fee for Private (VPC + on-prem) deployments, 2) a tiered support offering that scales with customer risk and SLA needs, and 3) recommended upgrade cadences and tooling for customer-managed upgrades. Parallelly, complete the enterprise security questionnaire (SOC-like / customer RFP responses) for three strategic prospects and fold any blocking asks into product/contract requirements.

Goal:
- Produce a pricing matrix and support playbook that Sales can use for deals from $50k to $2M ARR for Private deployments.
- Define upgrade/maintenance cadences and an optional paid-managed upgrade service.
- Close security questionnaire gaps for target prospects within 10 business days.

Scope:
- Private modes: VPC-hosted (Redwood-managed control plane, customer VPC), and on-prem (air-gapped installable package).
- Commercial constructs: one-time license fee (initial install), annual platform fee, optional managed services (upgrade, backup, DR), premium observability retention.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours email), Priority (24/7 incidents + SLA), Enterprise (dedicated TAM + white-glove onboarding).

Out of scope for this ticket: final legal language redlines (handled by Legal PRR flow), implementation of upgrade automation (engineering epic ENG-2999 will deliver).
acceptance_criteria: Finalized pricing matrix with at least 3 scenarios (SMB, Mid-market, Enterprise) and model inputs (GPU counts, nodes, data residency) documented.
Support tier definitions with target response and resolution SLAs and associated price multipliers.
Upgrade cadence recommendations (monthly security, quarterly minor, annual major) and an optional paid managed-upgrade plan mockup.
Completed security questionnaire responses for three named prospects and list of remaining product/legal action items.
Sales playbook draft with negotiation ranges and template contract term suggestions for license + support combos.
Telemetry plan for measuring price elasticity and deal economics instruments (discounts, add-ons) instrumented in Console/CRM.
proposed_pricing_matrix: SMB scenario: license fee = $25k one-time + $10k/year platform fee, supports up to 2 dedicated GPUs or equivalent; support = Standard included; estimated ARR range $50k-$75k.
Mid-market scenario: license fee = $150k one-time + $75k/year platform fee, supports up to 8 GPUs; support = Priority optional at +20% of annual fee; estimated ARR $225k-$350k.

Enterprise scenario: license fee = $450k one-time + $300k/year platform fee, supports >16 GPUs + advanced networking; support = Enterprise +15% of annual fee with optional TAM; estimated ARR $700k-$2M depending on managed services.
proposed_support_tiers: Standard: Business-hours email and ticketing, 48h initial response, best-effort incident support. Included in base annual platform fee.
Priority: 24/7 alerts ingestion, 4h initial response for Sev1, P1 escalation channel, phone on-call for incidents. Add-on priced at +20% of annual platform fee.

Enterprise: Dedicated Technical Account Manager, quarterly business reviews, custom runbooks, on-site option for upgrades, SLA-backed uptime crediting. Add-on priced at +15%-25% depending on size and TAM allocation.
upgrade_cadence_options: Security patches: monthly rolling patch releases; customers can opt for auto-apply (managed) or opt-in (self-managed).
Minor feature releases: quarterly cadence with 30-day opt-out window for customers that need freeze windows.
Major releases (breaking changes): annual, communicated 90 days in advance with migration guides and a paid managed-migration offering.
Emergency hotfix process: 24-72h turnaround for critical security fixes; managed-upgrade customers receive priority auto-install.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Weeks 1-3): run pricing workshops with Sales and Legal, finalize initial matrix and draft playbook.
Phase 2 (Weeks 4-6): pilot pricing with 3 active deals identified by Sales; collect elasticity and negotiation datapoints.
Phase 3 (Weeks 7-8): iterate on pricing/support tiers, finalize security questionnaire templates and handoffs to engineering/legal.
Phase 4 (Week 9): publish Sales playbook, enable checkout/ops onboarding checklist, and launch internal enablement session.
telemetry_requirements: Track closed-won vs. closed-lost for Private deals with pricing variant tag (license tier, support add-on, discount level).
Instrument Console onboarding funnel for private installs: time-to-first-successful-deploy, upgrade opt-in %, managed-upgrade conversions.
Capture customer tickets by category post-upgrade to measure churn/risk associated with release cadence.
Add fields in CRM to store "pricing_variant" and "managed_upgrade_opt_in" for cohort analysis.
legal_QA_open_items: Encryption at rest: confirm algorithm and customer KMS integration options; Legal requests side-letter template for required attestation.
Data residency: define acceptable region mapping and runbook for cross-region fallbacks; product needs to surface region constraint in onboarding.
Support SLA credits: Legal to approve formula for uptime credits tied to.Support tier P1 response/resolution metrics.
Indemnity & export controls: confirm with Legal and Security whether special clauses are required for on-prem air-gapped deployments in regulated sectors.
